text:
sam: Heads-up — seeing a spike of 502s hitting hostedapi in eu-west-1 for a subset of requests. Only noticed when caller sets X-Customer-Billing header. ~20% of requests fail with upstream reset. Anyone else seeing this?

maria: I see alerts too, Alert: hostedapi-eu1 gateway 502-rate up. Can you paste a sample request id / trace id?

sam: trace=trace-0a1b2c3d. curl test below reproduces locally:

sam: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Customer-Billing: acct_123" \
  "https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":10}'

* Connected to hosted.redwood.ai (54.12.34.56) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: hosted.redwood.ai
> <...>
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< {"error":"upstream reset by peer","trace":"trace-0a1b2c3d"}
```

leo: Grepping edge logs for that trace id — here's the envoy line: `envoy upstream reset: reset reason = connection termination, upstream host = gw-backend-12` and upstream 503/502 mapping. Also seeing `stream idle timeout` messages for a few requests.

ops-bot: [automated] hostedapi-eu1 gateway error rate increased 4x over baseline (last 5m). Ticket created: #INC-7932

maria: Any pattern in payload size or model type? Sam said small prompt. If it's header-specific maybe billing proxy is slow/dropping after header inspection.

sam: Confirmed small payloads only. I toggled `X-Customer-Billing` to a different value and errors stop. So looks correlated to a particular account id.

leo: Looking at midproxy and billing-proxy traces: the billing service is taking ~1.2s on that account id and sometimes aborts TCP mid-request under load (we have a 1s tail cutoff in the midproxy). That causes connection termination -> envoy converts to 502.

support-erica: Customer reported 502s in their SDK logs around 15:12 UTC. They've already escalated. Can we provide repro steps and a short mitigation?

maria: Repro steps: 1) curl with header X-Customer-Billing: acct_123 (sam provided). 2) Run 50 concurrent requests: `seq 1 50 | xargs -n1 -P10 -I{} curl -s -H "X-Customer-Billing: acct_123" ...` 3) Observe ~20% 502s.

sam: Quick mitigation: route that tenant away from billing-proxy path. Config patch we tested: set routing rule to bypass billing header-based enrichment for acct_123 -> route to fallback upstream pool `gw-backend-unvalidated`. Short term we can flip a flag in FastRouter.

leo: I pushed a canary that drops enrichment for acct_123 on eu-west-1 (10% traffic) — no increased 502s so far. If stable for 5m we'll promote to 100%.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] canary rollout started for route bypass: canary id rb-842, scope eu-west-1, 10%

maria: Postmortem notes for support: probable cause = billing-enrichment service for that account id causing TCP abort under concurrent load; upstream termination observed as 502 at edge. Secondary contributor: midproxy config had tight idle/termination thresholds that convert slow enrichment into aborts.

support-erica: Customer communication: Sorry, we're investigating elevated 502s for requests with X-Customer-Billing set. Workaround: remove header or reissue requests to eu-central-1 (we're routing them there temporarily). ETA for full fix TBD, will update in 30m.

leo: Follow-ups: - increase midproxy idle threshold to 3s (temp) - add retry on 502 for idempotent generate calls when header present (1 retry, exponential backoff) - add per-tenant circuit breaker on billing-proxy.

sam: After promoting canary to 100% (4867770280), error rate dropped to baseline.

ops-bot: [metrics] hostedapi-eu1 gateway 502-rate returned to normal at 4867770332

support-erica: Closing loop with customer. Will open a post-incident doc with repro steps and follow-ups.

maria: Filing PRs for midproxy threshold and routing rule cleanup. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sam: tl;dr: Billing enrichment for acct_123 caused midproxy abort -> envoy mapped to 502. Canary bypass fixed it.
